question.text: Under Section 12 of the PMLA, 2002, what is the record retention period for transaction records between a client and a reporting entity?

answer.text: Five years from the date of the transaction
Three years from the date of the transaction
Ten years from the date of the transaction
One year from the date of the transaction

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 12 of the PMLA, 2002, records of transactions must be maintained for five years from the date of the transaction. Client identity records are similarly retained for five years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed. The Trap: Ten years is tempting because some jurisdictions require longer retention; under Indian PMLA it is specifically five years. Note: The IFSCA Guidelines separately prescribe six years for their own records — a distinction worth keeping in mind.
